original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

actual_scope: On the PR2322 T74 words (the base of the open PR2349/PR2363/PR2374 line): what is the certified owner-fill headroom, and what is the exact LP-ceiling price of each realized or candidate local inventory move (PR2322 handoffs, PR2339 low/high aliases, rank-1 climb merges), with a census of untried PR2322-pattern handoff sites?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a new local cost interface can beat current packing. For the live T74 line the useful narrowing is to price concrete inventory moves on the actual PR2322 words with the width-aware LP, after showing packing itself is exhausted, so constructors can see which interface changes are worth building.
bottleneck_link: The complex supplier binds. On the PR2322 words, owner fills are within 8.1e-10 of a certified cap, so further T74 gains must come from local inventory or climb-shape changes; this package prices those moves exactly and points to the largest (rank-1 climb merges, +1.13e-7 each).
stop_rule: Stop after the certified cap, exact decomposition of the two realized changes, prices of four move types, an independent recount and the site census; no handoff construction in this session.
evidence: move_prices.py: per-register recount of 8 pinned words (each equal to its reported profile and inventory), exact decompositions PR2312->PR2322 and PR2269->PR2339, LP prices, calibration (LP +1.96e-7 vs realized +1.69e-7), certified cap b < 0.001697195759 for every legal whole-helper fill of the PR2322 words (PR2374 not rejected). independent_recount.py (separate implementation by an AI reviewer subagent) reproduces profiles, the change set and the site lists. merge_mechanism.py: all 26 PR2339 target merges come from removed helpers' early gates replaced by frame-0 initial corrections; frame-0 lender census {4:32, 7:8, 8:8, 9:240}; rank-zero aliases lose even with merge credit; higher-rank take-overs priced.

open_questions.question: Does helper 653 of the PR2322 words admit a PR2322-type coherent handoff to a free (5,1,1,1) X register with partners 648/649/650/652?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Block 53 has exactly PR2322's pre-handoff shape pattern; the move is priced at +4.27e-8, about a third of the whole PR2363->PR2374 owner gain.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun PR2322's handoff generator with role 653 and each of the 12 free (5,1,1,1) X registers as candidate lenders.
open_questions.blocked_by: PR2374 dropped alias 653 when moving 651 to lender 530; lender/lifetime conflicts are unchecked here.

open_questions.question: Can a frame-0 lender ending at dimension 7 or 8 take over a removed width-8 helper's role (higher-rank handoff), with the role's gate frames raised to contain the lender's frame?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Rank-zero anticipatory aliases (width-4 -> 9 lenders) lose even with the target merges credited; the 16 frame-0 lenders ending at dimension 7-8 are priced at up to +1.43e-6 per take-over on the PR2322 words before frame-raising costs.
open_questions.first_step: Build one such word with the PR2339 builder relaxing its condition (d), then recount it with move_prices.py's recount to price the actual reshape of the role and its partners.
open_questions.blocked_by: The handoff is outside the rank-zero K_G contract of PR2226/PR2339; legality, frame raising and native lowering are unproven.

open_questions.question: Which other (lender shape, partner shape) handoff patterns occurring in the PR2322 words have positive prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only (5,1,1,1) lenders are priced here; the 12 such registers limit PR2322-type handoffs to +5.1e-7.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate per-register shapes of all X registers and helpers and price each feasible-looking reshape pair with move_prices.applied().
open_questions.blocked_by: Legality of a handoff depends on frame availability and lifetimes that the pricing screen does not model.
